Cyber Manhunt is a pretty good game. The story is well-written, if a bit difficult to follow sometimes, and has a lot of good elements to it. There are flaws, however, and many of them interfere with the immersion. This review will be free of major spoilers, with only a few plot points hinted at. I won't ruin your play experience if you decide to buy it yourself.

In terms of visuals, the game looks great. The art and animation are well done and have their own unique style to them. The UI looks pretty great too, though there are problems there that lie beyond their sleek exteriors. One of the most annoying parts (something that could have been easily implemented, I'll bet) is that you can't use the TAB key to move between fields. The password cracker requires you to input several pieces of information in across multiple fields, and you'll do this several times in each case. You can't use TAB, though, so you pretty much have to do everything with your mouse. It's a minor gripe, but I found myself annoyed at these sections of the game. They included CTRL+C and CTRL+V, but not TAB?

Sound design is mixed. The music is great, from the actual lyrical songs, to the general background music. It's a little repetitive, but it fits the game and doesn't distract from what you're trying to do. I think the Reasoning music is my favorite just for how nice it sounds, adding a bit of urgency to the normal background music. The voice acting, however, is mixed at best. Some roles sound better than others, but the game would have benefited from better voice direction.

However, the story suffers the most, because whoever was in charge of localizing the game [i]seriously dropped the ball[/i]. The tutorial and first case (so the content included in the demo) have the best localization, but even then it's not great. The wording of hundreds of messages in the game is awkward and fake-sounding, some parts even sounding like those phishing e-mails written by the prince of Nigeria. There were places where the localization was downright unintelligible, and I ended up having to make guesses in certain parts of the game to progress the story because I couldn't make sense of the options provided.

The story itself, localization issues aside, is good, but feels disjointed at times. There are two major plots that run simultaneously, and they seem completely separate from each other, even when they should be working together. Also, characterization for the main NPC was just wrong - through other dialogue and flavor text, the game seems to be trying to establish this character as your friend, but they act distant at best and antagonistic at worst, so your motivations get muddled at certain parts of the story. Puzzle design is pretty good, though there are two or three puzzles that will practically force you to look up a guide because their design is pretty obtuse. But overall, the game has a good message about privacy in the digital age - it's just a bit hampered by the way the game is presented.

Overall, Cyber Manhunt is a good, but flawed game. After playing other hacking games like Code7, Hacknet, and Uplink, I found it to be more on the point-and-click adventure side of things rather than an actual hacking simulator, but it really needed a final layer of polish if it wanted to be one of the greats in the genre. I think the game's overall appeal would be greatly increased by having a good localization team go through and fix a lot of the rough translations and making the game more accessible and immersive.

The game really can't decide if it wants to be puzzly or hold your hand constantly, even artificially blocking your progression until it deems you "ready".

It adds up to a LOT of time wasted, even if you aren't forced to repeat them because of the random minute "quizzes" the game occasionally throws at you, marking the only time where the game won't let you look up anything. You remember exactly WHERE the info would be, but no - you have to game over, retry, look it up, go through 1 or 2 minutes of unskippable very mediocre voiced lines again, and only THEN are you allowed to progress... to the next question. Rinse and repeat, unless you literally memorized every single little remark and detail from dozens of random conversations and social media posts.

The game ist just so incredibly tedious to play. It actively doesn't want you to have any fun. The story could be decent enough I guess, but it's certainly not enough of a payoff for the awful, awful gameplay.

Really wish I could recommend this game but the bugs and poor translation ruin what would have otherwise been a cool experience. Ran into two game breaking bugs, one fixed after a reset and the other remains to be fixed, in the last chapter. After solving a puzzle the game reverts back to a state before the puzzle was solved, while the timer continues to countdown.

Another huge problem, especially in the last chapter, is the game is throwing a ton of background lore at you while an onscreen timer ticks away, in a scenario where the game can't even be paused. The interface already makes it hard to quickly grab information, but now you have to grab it while racing the clock, and solving puzzles. Your option is either to go slow and actually absorb the lore (failing and having to repeat after multiple attempts), or go quickly and miss anything story related. 

The concept of this game is great and almost done well here. ALMOST. It needs better translation and better writing, way less bugs and a better UI. Whether it was script or direction, the voice acting was not up to par either.

Playing for so long only for the game to break at the end really soured me on it, but I'm hoping the devs can fix it for their next iteration, because there is definite potential here.

I bought this game months ago because it was cheap (I believe it was on sale at the time) and completely forgot about it until now. I went into this game with not knowing what to expect, and now I am addicted to it. I think it is a perfect game for those who like to find clues and solve mysteries. I can see how this could be boring for some other people since all you do is clicking different buttons on the screen to find clues. However, the back stories are very interesting and I think that alone make this game worth playing.

I do have some criticisms for this game though. When I was trying to complete the first chapter, the game kept telling I have one more clue to find, I looked up guides online and saw that I already found everything. I figured it was a bug and had to restart the chapter. Some of the voice acting also feel a bit unnatural, it's almost like the voice actors were just reading from the script which kind of threw me off. In a few dialogues, what the voice actors said also did not match the subtitle, which is fine if they have the same meaning but for example, there is one part where the subtitle said "hacker" while the voice actor said "leader" which feels a bit off since the character we play as isn't really a "leader". I am also not too crazy about the illustrations, some of the characters' anatomy look weird and not consistent (when there are 3 illustrations of the same character from different angles, they almost look like 3 different people) I do like how painterly it looks but in some areas they used actual photos with a filter while some of them they kept the painterly illustrations which is a bit odd.

Nevertheless for me, it was a game worth playing and I definitely would be interested to check out the DLCs and the next game after this one.

Pros: I enjoyed the gameplay since it reminded me of the Orwell games and the investigation and twists reminded me of a Ace Attorney game. The story is pretty good as its combined into 5 or so chapters where you have to find out what happened to a certain person why this person was killed. So if you're a fan of detective games like LA Noir, this definitely a good game to buy. Also it adds some pretty heavy topics that may be triggering for some people but I feel like it was a good attempt at trying to address them.

Cons: With all the pros, theres some things that really bug me about this game. 

[list]
    [*]Story - As I said, the story is really good and the investigation keeps you engrossed to find out what exactly happened or led to the incident that took place. But around Chapter 4, the game shifts from a political/suspense thriller to a weird sci-fi "Deus Ex" type story. It really didn't mesh well with me in trying to connect all the previous chapters. And this is around the same part where the main antagonist gets introduced. And by God is this one of the most over-dramatic mustache twirling villains I've ever seen. Their backstory is slightly explored in one of the DLCs but even then it doesn't really help to justify their actions in the main campaign nor those it add any really depth to their character. The only sub-antagonist that got any type of depth and I went "Oh wow, I can see why they did this" was [spoiler] Lisa Snyder [/spoiler] in Chapter 1 and returned in one of the DLC chapters which in turn made the later my favorite chapter. 
   
 [*]Puzzles - I don't normally criticize puzzles because I dont want to come off as that guy that cant do puzzles because I'm too dumb or whatever. But I'll take that risk for this game. Some of the puzzles and mini games here are difficult to a frustrating degree. Mainly because I felt there was little hints given to me on how to solve them. And this definitely goes for the mini games. There's one at the very end of the last DLC chapter that was so hard, I pretty much just gave up after going at it for an hour or two and just watched the ending on YouTube. One of the walkthroughs I found online even made the statement that some of the puzzles were not explained well so I'm gonna guess its not just me who feels this way.
   
 [*]Voices - While the DLC chapters are fully voiced, I suspect some of the main campaign voices are synthetic and were maybe spoken by AI generated software [spoiler] A bit ironic considering the story of the game [/spoiler]. For the most part it sounds ok but some words come out very weird. 
[/list]



Summary: Cyber Manhunt is a good game and very much worth the price you pay for it. But the weird Deus Ex story keeps me from fully enjoying it. Had it stuck with the political/corporate drama of Company X trying to sway and control the population through Big Data, I would've absolutely loved it. It really did not need the Deus Ex element and should've been completely left out. And when you do take it out of the game, it really doesn't take a whole lot away from the story, so its strange as to why it was even added in the first place.

Cyber Manhunt falls disappointingly short of what I was expecting. While it's evident that the developers poured time and effort into this game, the end result is a mediocre experience. Nothing is horribly bad, but nothing is great either.

One of the major letdowns is the story line, which is... cliched. I could figure out where it was going almost beat-for-beat. The characters feel two-dimensional, and most of the time I could skip past their dialogue and just find the highlighted bits I was meant to find without losing anything meaningful from the parts I skipped. 
Sleuthing, he game's core mechanic, turns out to be a painfully limited and repetitive experience. The investigative elements promised are reduced to basic point-and-click tasks, and copy-and-pasting things into boxes. The puzzles lack complexity and fail to challenge the player's intellect, resulting a cycle that gets old after chapter 2.
The dialogue delivery is often wooden, making it difficult to immerse oneself in the story.

I can tell the devs really tried, which redeems this to a point, but the overall experience falls flat. With a more engaging story line and more diverse detective mechanics, Cyber Manhunt could have been a standout title.

While it's evident that the developers poured time and effort into this game, the end result is a mediocre experience. Nothing is horribly bad, but nothing is great either. One of the major letdowns is the story line, which is... cliched. I could figure out where it was going almost beat-for-beat. The characters feel two-dimensional, and most of the time I could skip past their dialogue and just find the highlighted bits I was meant to find without losing anything meaningful from the parts I skipped. Sleuthing, he game's core mechanic, turns out to be a painfully limited and repetitive experience. The investigative elements promised are reduced to basic point-and-click tasks, and copy-and-pasting things into boxes. The puzzles lack complexity and fail to challenge the player's intellect, resulting a cycle that gets old after chapter 2. The dialogue delivery is often wooden, making it difficult to immerse oneself in the story. I can tell the devs really tried, which redeems this to a point, but the overall experience falls flat. With a more engaging story line and more diverse detective mechanics, Cyber Manhunt could have been a standout title.

review_text_raw: The concept of the game is great. The Narrative is interesting, but you have to go so fast that you don't really get to enjoy the story. The mechanics of the game are terrible. Playing on a laptop with a trackpad/clicker, I spent way too much time pushing the various windows around trying to get the right window that had the info that I needed. When you have to go so fast, you don't have time for all the opening, closing, pushing windows around. Also, having to look up the same info twice in different chapters of the game is silly, because a real computer-based detective would have had it already. But overall, I enjoyed using the many digital forms of hacking info, cracking codes, and piecing together the story. I like the way the game brought in social media influencers too, that felt very 'real'.  Another critique is that the game is very violent in parts, violent stories of torture, rape and killing; demeaning to women on the whole.There is no need for it to be so violent; it doesn't make it a better story. For that, I would not recommend it.
